name: HyperTheft
impact: Untrusted host reads the deterministic-encryption ciphertext side channel of a TEE-shielded neural network and reconstructs functionality-equivalent model weights from a single execution
mitigation: No patch for the channel: deterministic encryption is a design choice of the TEE, so hardware-level countermeasures are required
boundary_statement: HyperTheft (CCS 2024) recovers DNN weights from the ciphertext side channel created by deterministic memory encryption, achieving 77-97% test accuracy from one execution. Attacks were demonstrated on AMD SEV and the paper states they are 'feasible to any deterministic-encryption-based TEEs'; only the SEV mapping is tagged as confirmed.

AMD-SEV-SNP.evidence: Paper: 'Practical attacks have been demonstrated on AMD SEV and reported to the vendor; yet, the attacks are feasible to any deterministic-encryption-based TEEs.'

INTENT.evidence: The paper names AMD SEV, ARM CCA and Intel TDX as deterministic-encryption TEEs; only SEV is reported as demonstrated, so the other two are not tagged.
